title: Collections Note: Figuring the Detour Toll Return on Wayfare Rides
content:
**Amount.** The detour toll return on a trip of **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)** is the attributed toll multiplied by the facility weight, then by the member tenure multiplier, then by the toll timeliness factor, with the fare-size allowance then added in dollars; it never exceeds the toll charged on the trip and is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end.

**Attributed toll.** The toll charged on the trip times the detour toll share of 0.25 (25 percent).

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Detour toll share | 0.25 of the toll charged on the trip |
| Facility weight | 0.4 |
| Member tenure multiplier | 1.0 |
| Toll timeliness factor | 1.0 |
| Fare-size allowance | nil ($0.00) |
| Ceiling | the toll charged on the trip |

## How the figure is built

- The toll charged on the trip is the toll charge amount booked on the trip.
- The attributed toll is multiplied by the facility weight, the member tenure multiplier and the toll timeliness factor in turn; nothing is rounded along the way.
- The fare-size allowance is added in dollars after the multiplications, never multiplied.
- The total is held at or below the toll charged on the trip, and only then rounded half up to the cent.

## Worked examples (hypothetical tolls)

*Toll of $4.30.* Attributed toll: $4.30 times 0.25 is $1.075. Multiplied by 0.4 is $0.43; by 1.0 and by 1.0 it stays $0.43; plus $0.00. Below the $4.30 ceiling: **$0.43**.

*Toll of $2.10.* Attributed toll $0.525; multiplied by 0.4 is $0.21; the return is **$0.21**.
